name: CT-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: Entrenched Democratic incumbent in a D+8 district
Overwhelming fundraising edge: $1.6M raised vs. roughly $15K for the Republican
Prediction markets price the race near 97% Democratic
No public polls or expert ratings; outlook rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: An entrenched incumbent in a district leaning eight points Democratic faces a challenger who has raised barely one percent of her total, and markets price the race near 97 percent Democratic. With no polling suggesting competition, the seat remains safely Democratic.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against DeLauro or a broader polling miss in similar New England districts could narrow the expected margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Rosa DeLauro, the Democratic incumbent, seeks re-election in a Connecticut district that leans Democratic by eight points. Her campaign has raised about $1.6 million and holds a large cash advantage, while Republican Chris Lancia has reported roughly $15,000 in receipts. No public polls of the general election are available, and no expert raters have published assessments of the race. Prediction markets price the Democratic chance at about 97 percent.

With no direct polling, the outlook rests on district partisanship, incumbency, and the lopsided money race, all of which favor DeLauro. Independent candidate Thomas Egan is on the ballot but reports no fundraising or measurable support. The expected margin is roughly twenty-one points for DeLauro, with uncertainty widened by the absence of survey data. Any serious challenge would require a late shift not currently visible in the evidence.
